        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><h2>Bump minimum Java version to 17</h2>
<p>Java 17 was released almost 5 years ago. Since the migration between post-8 versions does not bring as much pain as the migration from 8 to 11, it was decided to bump minimum Java version to 17. There are dependencies (like Jetty) that require Java 17 or higher. You can still compile your project with Java 11, but then when you need to run TeaVM with at least Java 17.</p>
<p>TeaVM public dependencies like JSO still compatible with Java 11.</p>
<h2>New compiler extension API</h2>
<p>Previously, TeaVM allowed describing the list of reflectable entries by extending <code>ReflectionSupplier</code> class and registering it using <code>ServiceLoader</code> convention. The problem with this approach was that the <code>ReflectionSupplier</code> API relied on compiler internals, which are not guaranteed to be stable.</p>
<p>0.15.0 introduces new public user-friendly API for introspecting compiler structures in reflection-style way. It does not include any compiler modules as dependencies. Additionally, this API adds more user-friendly fluent configuration, for example:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-java notranslate position-relative overflow-auto"><pre><span class="pl-en">selectClasses</span>(<span class="pl-en">withAnnotation</span>(<span class="pl-smi">MyReflectable</span>.<span class="pl-k">class</span>))
    .<span class="pl-en">reflectablePublicMembers</span>()
    .<span class="pl-en">foundByName</span>();</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container position-absolute right-0 top-0">

<p>Together with reflection definitions, there are two new extension points: <code>ResourcePolicy</code> and <code>SubstibutionPolicy</code>. The former allows to control which resources are included in the final bundle. The latter allows to substitute certain classes with TeaVM-specific implementation. Primary goal is to provide web-friendly implementations of classes that rely heavily on native routines.</p>
<p>Old APIs are now deprecated. Moreover, former <code>META-INF/teavm.properties</code> approach is no more supported: it was never documented and never considered public.</p>
<h2>Improvements to reflection</h2>
<p>Following APIs added:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>java.lang.reflect.Proxy</code></li>
<li><code>java.lang.reflect.Executable#getParameterAnnotations</code></li>
<li><code>java.lang.reflect.Executable#getExceptionTypes</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Also, this version fixes a bug with calling async methods via reflection.</p>
<h2>Improvements to Wasm GC backend</h2>
<h3>New internal representation for Wasm instructions</h3>
<p>TeaVM added support for WebAssembly in early pre-MVP stages. Back then early proposals relied on expression-based (tree) syntax for method bodies. Later, the committee change it with instruction-based (flat) syntax, but TeaVM never had a chance to switch to this one, performing conversion right at the stage of WebAssembly binary format emission. Now, TeaVM finally closes this gap and represents WebAssembly instructions as is, which allows more efficient code generation.</p>
<p>As an example, TeaVM starts utilizing <code>local.tee</code> instruction instead of pairs of <code>local.set</code>/<code>local.get</code>, which in turn can decrease module size by up to 1%.</p>
<h3>Replace <code>try</code> with <code>try_table</code> instruction</h3>
<p>Exception handling support in WebAssembly had made a thorny way, with at least one deprecation. TeaVM witnessed this and stuck at the former (now deprecated) way to encode exceptions. Now TeaVM closes this gap as well and starts emitting new exception handling instruction. As a consequence, you will notice that Firefox does not log warnings when loading Wasm modules, produced by TeaVM.</p>
<h2>Stop bundling TeaVM with IDEA plugin</h2>
<p>Previously, TeaVM IDEA plugin bundled full TeaVM. This made it impossible to sit on recent IDEA plugin versions (actually, IDEA always suggests to upgrade to the most recent one), while having a Maven/Gradle project of a bit older version. Now, IDEA plugin downloads TeaVM on demand, taking the version that is used in the project.</p>
<p>This improvement has one small issue though: this all works ONLY starting 0.15.0. So, you can't install TeaVM IDEA plugin version 0.15.0 and use it to build, for example, 0.14.1. But as soon as your IDEA plugin is updated to 0.16.0 and so on, you'll still be able to build with 0.15.0.</p>
<h2>Other improvements</h2>
<ul>
<li>Support for <code>java.lang.ref.Cleaner</code></li>
<li>Fix dev server Gradle tasks compatible with configuration cache</li>
<li>Add Jetbrains' <code>@Language</code> annotation to <code>@JSBody</code>, so that JavaScript in <code>@JSBody</code> is highlighted in IDEA.</li>
<li>add <code>debug</code> property to Gradle configuration to turn on all debugging properties in one shot.</li>
</ul>

You can join these people and start supporting the project.</p></div>

        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><h2>Refactoring reflection support</h2>
<p>Reflection support was first introduced in ancient era of TeaVM, when only JavaScript backend was available.<br>
It was not designed to be cross-platform, so when other backends were added, they brought their own vision<br>
of how reflection should work. This made the code base more code smell and prevented from the introduction<br>
of new features in reflection. This release comes with huge refactoring of reflection, now all backends<br>
sharing the same common concepts.</p>
<h2>Improving reflection support</h2>
<p>The reflection refactoring allowed to improve reflection support in several ways:</p>
<ul>
<li>Add support for generic types</li>
<li>Add support for annotations on fields and methods</li>
<li>Add some support in C backend</li>
</ul>
<h2>Removal of old WebAssembly backends</h2>
<p>Old (non-GC) WebAssembly backend, as well as WASI backend, were removed from the project.<br>
They failed to gain any adoption. In the meantime Web WebAssembly GC surpasses WebAssembly MVP in all aspects.<br>
Also, WebAssembly GC has gained immediate adoption after first publication a couple of years ago.<br>
This makes it pointless to invest time into these backends, so they were removed.</p>
<h2>Integration with emscripten</h2>
<p>Wasm GC backend comes with new feature: now it's <a href="/konsoletyper/teavm/blob/0.14.0/docs/wasm-gc-backend/emscripten.html">possible</a> to dynamically<br>
link TeaVM-generated module with emscripten-generated module. Unlike naive approach when<br>
modules just loaded independently and see each other via Wasm imports, this new linking mechanism<br>
runs both modules in the same Wasm linear memory, which opens the opportunity to pass large binary blocks<br>
between C/C++ code and Java code.</p>
<h2>Other improvements</h2>
<ul>
<li>Cleanup unnecessary technical frames in stack traces, generated by Wasm GC deobfuscator</li>
<li>Allow to rewrite native methods with pluggable Metaprogramming generators</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<p>Finally, a big thank you to <a href="https://akwatype.io/community" rel="nofollow">Oki{ine</a> and <a href="https://github.com/shannah">@shannah</a>,<br>
for sponsoring the project as well as other sponsors (see <a href="https://github.com/sponsors/konsoletyper">full list</a>).<br>
You can join these people and start supporting the project.</p></div>

        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><p>This release contains bugfixes for 0.13.0, including:</p>
<ul>
<li>Wasm GC: Workaround WebAssembly bugs in Safari</li>
<li>Wasm GC: prevent backend from generation of annotations for special runtime classes - this caused validation errors in some cases when using reflection</li>
<li>Fix processing of bytecode with unreachable basic blocks</li>
<li>Don't report error when casting to an unsupported class - in this case cast does not have a chance to succeed, so no compile-time error necessary</li>
<li>Wasm GC: fix identity hash code on objects when they are used for synchronization</li>
<li>Wasm GC: fix incorrect bit mask, applied to identity hash code, so that now it uses 31 bits instead of 27 prior</li>
<li>C: fix compilation on Windows</li>
<li>Prevent generation of reflection metadata for fields and methods that aren't described as reflectable</li>
<li>Fix bug in <code>Random.nextLong</code></li>
<li>C: fix incorrect uninitialized values observed in exception handlers in some cases</li>
<li>C: fix bugs in direct NIO buffers</li>
<li>Fix behaviour of <code>containsAll</code>, called on <code>Collections.emptySet()</code></li>
<li>JS: fix creation of multidimensional byte arrays.</li>
<li>Fix running JUnit tests on Gradle 9.3</li>
<li>Wasm GC: fix generation of invalid Wasm module for some async methods.</li>
</ul>
<p>Special thanks to <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/lax1dude/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/lax1dude" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">@lax1dude</a> and <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/xpenatan/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/xpenatan" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">@xpenatan</a> for contributing fixes for some of these bugs</p></div>

        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><p>This release was driver by three major features in mind.</p>
<ol>
<li>Refactor to run in the browser</li>
<li>Coroutines</li>
<li>Java 25</li>
</ol>
<p>First is the (successful) attempt to create Java-to-WebAssembly compiler right in the browser. The work was done mostly outside TeaVM, but also required some refactorings in TeaVM core. You can see the result here: <a href="https://teavm.org/playground.html" rel="nofollow">https://teavm.org/playground.html</a></p>
<p>Second is closing final gap between JS and Wasm GC backend, which is coroutine support. TeaVM emulates Java threads via coroutines, which are only supported by JS backend. Version 0.13 introduces support for coroutines in Wasm GC, so now it's possible to call methods like <code>Thread.start</code> or <code>Thread.sleep</code>, use simple synchronization primitives and so on.</p>
<p>Finally, recently released Java 25 is supported.</p>
<p>Also, few minor features can be highlighted:</p>
<ul>
<li>Support for imported memory and <code>SharedArrayBuffer</code>. This allows, for example, to run a WebAssembly module in a worker and exchange data with it without the need to copy anything.</li>
<li>Support Node.js out-of-the-box</li>
</ul>
<p>Special thanks for helping to test the new release to:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/xpenatan/gdx-teavm">libGDX TeaVM</a> project and personally to <a href="https://github.com/xpenatan">@xpenatan</a>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/webfx-project/webfx">WebFX</a> project and personally to <a href="https://github.com/salmonb">@salmonb</a>.  This project allows to port JavaFX apps to the browser, using various compilers (GWT, j2cl), and now they added TeaVM support.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/zlataovce">@zlataovce</a> and his <a href="https://github.com/run-slicer/slicer">slicer</a>, which is a collection of Java bytecode decompilers, ported to the browser. Now these decompilers work in WebAssembly.</li>
</ul>
<p>Also, thanks to the contributors:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/electrum">@electrum</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/colorizenl">@colorizenl</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/tran4o">@tran4o</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/AsheraCordova">@AsheraCordova</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/lax1dude">@lax1dude</a></li>
</ul>
<p>Finally, a big thank you to <a href="https://github.com/reportmill/">@reportmill</a> and <a href="https://github.com/shannah">@shannah</a>, for sponsoring the project as well as other sponsors (see <a href="https://github.com/sponsors/konsoletyper">full list</a>). You can join these people and start supporting the project.</p></div>

        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><p>This release contains hotfixes for release 0.12.0</p>
<ul>
<li>Fix the default output dir for tests when running from Gradle</li>
<li>Fix the issue with the translation of try/catch statements in WebAssembly GC</li>
<li>Fix setting debug info location via Gradle plugin DSL</li>
<li>Fix setting NIO buffer position after relative bulk transfer</li>
<li>Fix issue in ZipFile implementation, see <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="2539931750" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/konsoletyper/teavm/issues/954" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/konsoletyper/teavm/issues/954/hovercard" href="https://github.com/konsoletyper/teavm/issues/954" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">#954</a></li>
<li>Fix error stack traces not reported properly in out-of-process mode</li>
<li>When devirtualizing during inlining, check that the target method is not abstract</li>
</ul></div>

        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><p>The main driver for this release was making WebAssembly GC backend on par with JavaScript backend. Now, only one feature of the JavaScript backend is not supported in Wasm GC: threading. This will be addressed in future releases.</p>
<p>Here's the list of improvements to the backend:</p>
<ol>
<li>Reflection support. It's far from being full, but now all features, supported in JavaScript, are also supported in WebAssembly GC.</li>
<li>Improved generation of virtual tables. Little optimization techniques were implemented to reduce the size of virtual tables generated for large projects.</li>
<li>Reduced size of overhead, produced for various types of arrays. Actually, there's no more overhead: all object array types share the same code. This can cause insignificant performance loss in favour of a significantly smaller binary size in large projects.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/WebAssembly/js-string-builtins/blob/main/proposals/js-string-builtins/Overview.md">JS string builtins proposal</a> is now used when available (for now it's only unsupported in Safari), which significantly improves string interchange between Java and native JS APIs.</li>
</ol>
<p>Another big change worth mentioning is the refactoring of NIO buffers. It was also driven <em>mostly</em> by the need of JS interop in Wasm GC backend, but as a result, all other backends benefit from this improvement. While previously NIO buffers were backed by arrays, now each backend uses more appropriate implementation. This includes typed arrays in JavaScript BE and direct memory addresses in C and old WebAssembly backends. Also, direct buffers in C are now allocated using <code>malloc</code> and using dedicated allocator in Wasm GC, that uses Wasm memory.</p>
<p>The latter change allows overcoming one major limitation of WebAssembly GC proposal: the inability to represent WebAssebmly array type as a JavaScript typed array. WebAssembly memory <em>can</em> be represented directly as a JavaScript typed array. So the solution is to allocate direct buffers over WebAssembly memory and then pass NIO buffers directly to JavaScript without any copying. In this regard JSO now allows passing NIO buffers directly to JavaScript. In this case they will be seen as a type array or as an ArrayBufferView respectively.</p>
<p>When this is not an option, though, and JS interop needs to fall back to copying data between arrays, it's now done via WebAssembly memory. Although one extra copy needs to be performed, the overall performance is <em>times</em> better than copying through WebAssebmly/JS barrier.</p>
<p>To make code re-usable between JavaScript and WebAssembly while still benefiting from the ability to pass data without copying, <code>@JSByRef</code> annotation gets <code>optional</code> parameter. "Optional by-ref" means that any backend that supports it (namely, JavaScript) passes data by reference, while others (WebAssembly GC) copies data.</p>
<p>Special thanks to <a href="https://libgdx.com/" rel="nofollow">libGDX</a> project and personally to <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/xpenatan/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/xpenatan" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">@xpenatan</a> for testing WebAssembly GC backend with their <a href="https://github.com/xpenatan/gdx-teavm">TeaVM backend</a>, which gave the opportunity to find and fix some bugs. Also, thanks to contributors:</p>

<li><a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/Ihromant/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/Ihromant" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">@Ihromant</a></li>

        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><h2>New WebAssembly backend</h2>
<p>This release is mostly driven by development of new WebAssembly backend. Old WebAssembly backend exists for many years and works well, however, did not see any adoption. The main reason is that it does not add significant advantages (like performance improvements), but makes development experience much worse, i.e. does not allow to easily interact with browser JS APIs and produces large binary files (times as large as JS).</p>
<p>With introduction of new WebAssembly GC proposal these problems were solved. However, this is not just small addition to original WebAssembly spec, but a game changer, it was impossible just to improve existing backend to support new proposal. So the decision was made to create a brand new WebAssembly backend, which would co-exist with the old one. Perhaps, at some point old WebAssembly backend will be deprecated and fully removed, but for now they will co-exist. However, WebAssembly GC will be advertised as primary WebAssembly target and the documentation will be maintained for WebAssembly GC, not for old WebAssembly.</p>
<p>New WebAssembly GC is a bit limited compared to JS backend, but mostly provides all features available in old WebAssembly backend. Moreover, WebAssembly GC fully supports JSO, as Java-to-JS interaction API. Hopefully, the next release will cover remaining features and WebAssembly GC backend will be on par with JS backend and the "experimental" tag will be removed from WebAssembly support.</p>
<h2>Java class library emulation</h2>
<ul>
<li>Fixed bugs in <code>BitSet</code> implementation</li>
<li>Add <code>ceilDiv</code>, <code>ceilDivExact</code>, <code>ceilMod</code>, <code>floorDivExact</code>, <code>absExact</code> to <code>Math</code> class.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Support for JS APIs</h2>
<ul>
<li>Reading files from <code><input type="file"></code>, which includes classes like <code>File</code>, <code>Blob</code>, <code>ReadableStream</code> and so on.</li>
<li>Binding for <code>HTMLElement.touch</code> and <code>HTMLElement.input</code> events.</li>
<li>Binding for <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API" rel="nofollow">Popover API</a>.</li>
<li>Binding for <code>Navigator.sendBeacon</code></li>
<li>Binding for <code>Error.cause</code></li>
</ul>
<h2>Other stuff</h2>
<ul>
<li>Long emulation was removed from JS runtime. Now JS only relies on  <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/BigInt" rel="nofollow">BigInt</a>,   which is supported by all browsers for more than 4 years.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Sponsorship</h2>
<p>Worth mentioning that TeaVM evolved with the support from its sponsors. If you like this project, you can <a href="https://github.com/sponsors/konsoletyper">start donating</a>.</p>
<p>Special thanks to <a href="https://github.com/reportmill/">@reportmill</a> and <a href="https://github.com/shannah">@shannah</a>, our permanent sponsors!</p>

</ul>
<p>Special thanks to <a href="https://github.com/Ihromant">@Ihromant</a>, <a href="https://github.com/lax1dude">@lax1dude</a> and <a href="https://github.com/xpenatan">xpenatan</a>, who were early adopters of WebAssembly GC backend and helped to find some bugs there. Also, I want to highlight <a href="https://github.com/lax1dude">@lax1dude</a>, who not only enabled WebAssembly GC in his project, bug managed to identify, fix and successfully sent his PR to main repository.</p></div>

        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><h2>Improvements to native JavaScript interaction</h2>
<h3>Exporting declarations from Java to JavaScript</h3>
<p>This long expected feature is finally delivered by this release. Now TeaVM can not only take standard Java main classes with main methods, but also <em>module</em> classes.  Instead of <code>main</code> method, they can declare <code>static</code> methods annotated with <code>@JSExport</code>.<br>
These methods will be exported from generated TeaVM module (or rather as top-level declarations in non-module output).</p>
<p>Additionally, <code>@JSExport</code> annotation can be used to mark methods of classes that should be available in JS. See full documentation in <a href="/konsoletyper/teavm/blob/0.10.0/docs/runtime/js-modules.html">Creating JavaScript modules</a> section.</p>
<h3>Generating modules</h3>
<p>From this release, TeaVM can produce ES2015 modules. Moreover, there's a new build parameter that allows to specify module type (CommonJS, ES2015, UMD, immediately-invoked function).</p>
<h3>Importing constructors</h3>
<p>Previously, to declare a constructor for a JS class, you had to define static factory method, annotated with <code>@JSBody</code> and some JS within. Now, it's possible to declare a non-abstract overlay class (should be additionally annotated with <code>@JSClass</code>) with constructors. To instantiate such classes, you can use <code>new</code> syntax, as you used for normal Java classes.</p>
<h3>Importing static and top-level methods</h3>
<p>Since this release, you can define <code>static native</code> methods of overlay classes without extra annotations. These methods will be automatically mapped to corresponding static JS methods.</p>
<p>You can also put <code>@JSTopLevel</code> annotation on such methods so that they aren't mapped to static methods of containing classes, but to top-level methods.</p>
<h3>Support <code>instanceof</code></h3>
<p>Overlay classes now properly support <code>instanceof</code> and casts (in strict mode). Note that <code>instanceof</code> is not available for interfaces (i.e. as previously, always produces <code>true</code>). Support of <code>instanceof</code> can be disabled for classes by applying <code>@JSClass(transparent = true)</code>.</p>
<h3>Importing declarations from external modules</h3>
<p>You can also use <code>@JSModule</code> annotation to import declarations from JS modules. Following cases possible:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>@JSModule</code> on class – imports class</li>
<li><code>@JSModule</code> and <code>@JSTopLevel</code> – imports function</li>
<li><code>@JSModule</code>, <code>@JSTopLevel</code> and <code>@JSProperty</code> – imports property</li>
</ul>
<h3>Support varargs</h3>
<p>Varargs methods of overlay classes now automatically mapped to varargs methods in JS.</p>
<h2>Improved string representation</h2>
<p>This release has changed the way <code>java.lang.String</code> represented internally. Instead of array of <code>char</code>, <code>java.lang.String</code> now contains field of native JS string. This can improve performance in some cases, most likely in calls to native JS methods. Previously, to convert <code>java.lang.String</code> to and from JS method, a full copy should have been made. Now, TeaVM only wraps/unwraps JS string with <code>java.lang.String</code> implementation, which is much faster.</p>
<p>This also improves debugging experience. Previously, if you open a <code>java.lang.String</code> value in browser dev tools, you had a object, which has a field, which is an object in turn, which wraps <code>UInt16Array</code>. Now, you only have to deal with one level of indirection (object that has a field), and an actual representation is not array of char codes, but JS string, easily readable in dev tools.</p>
<h2>ES2015 modules</h2>
<p>Since this release, TeaVM generates ES2015 output, not ES5. This allows not only to support ES2015 modules, but reduces output side thanks to arrow function syntax.</p>
<h2>Class library emulation</h2>
<ul>
<li><code>String.toLowerCase</code>/<code>toUpperCase</code> methods that take <code>Locale</code> parameter</li>
<li><code>chars</code> and <code>codePoints</code> methods in <code>CharSequence</code></li>
<li><code>String.format</code>/<code>Formatter.format</code> now support more format specifiers</li>
<li><code>Math</code> methods for arithmetic operations that throw exception on overflow</li>
<li><code>OutputStream.nullOutputStream</code></li>
<li><code>SecureRandom</code></li>
<li><code>BigInteger.sqrt</code></li>
<li><code>WeakHashMap</code></li>
<li><code>CopyOnWriteArrayList</code></li>
<li>Fair support of <code>ThreadLocal</code> in green threads</li>
<li>Support <code>@Inherited</code> annotations</li>
<li><code>PrintStream</code> implements <code>Appendable</code></li>
<li><code>BufferedReader.lines</code> method</li>
</ul>
<h2>Gradle plugin improvements</h2>
<ul>
<li>Improve source file resolution when generating source maps in Gradle</li>
<li>Add tasks to start/update and stop development server</li>
</ul>
<h2>Other stuff</h2>
<ul>
<li>Overlay class for JS <code>Promise</code> (<code>JSPromise</code> class)</li>
<li>Support <code>@Inherited</code> annotations</li>
<li>New convention for event registration in standard overlay classes (on<strong>EventName</strong>  returning <code>Registration</code> to unbind the listener, instead of listen<strong>EventName</strong>/neglect<strong>EventName</strong>).</li>
</ul>
<h2>Sponsorship</h2>
<p>Worth mentioning that TeaVM evolved with the support from its sponsors. If you like this project, you can <a href="https://github.com/sponsors/konsoletyper">start donating</a>.</p>
<p>Special thanks to <a href="https://github.com/reportmill/">@reportmill</a> and <a href="https://github.com/shannah">@shannah</a>, our permanent sponsors!</p>

        <div data-pjax="true" data-test-selector="body-content" data-view-component="true" class="markdown-body tmp-my-3"><p>This release contains hotfixes for release 0.9.0</p>
<ul>
<li>Fix Maven archetype</li>
<li>Fix declaration in IndexedDB API</li>
<li>Fixes for wrapping JS values into Java objects</li>
<li>Fix issue in optimizing floating-point comparison operations (<code>fcmpg</code>, <code>fcmpl</code>, <code>dcmpg</code>, <code>dcmpl</code>)<br>
in corner-cases like NaN or negative zero</li>
<li>Fix bug in <code>LinkedHashMap</code> that could lead to inconsistent state in some cases</li>
<li>Fix boxing/unboxing arguments and return values in method references</li>
<li>Widen byte/short to ints in <code>ObjectMethods</code> emulation</li>
<li>Fix issue in <code>InputStreamReader</code> that lead to infinite loop in some cases</li>
</ul>
<p>Special thanks to <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/SquidDev/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/SquidDev" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">@SquidDev</a> who contributed commit to this release.</p>
<p>Note that due to mistake version <code>0.9.1</code> was published with incorrect content.<br>
Please, ignore it.</p></div>
